lines: Luis paid a handyman $2,400 this year.

beats.note: Paid by credit card or a payment network? That goes on a 1099-K, not your 1099-NEC.

beats.kicker: Due to contractors and the IRS

beats.sub: Who gets one, W-9 tracker, 2027 deadlines.

captions.instagram:
The 1099-NEC rule changed for payments you make in 2026.

✔️ The threshold is now $2,000 for the year, up from $600.
✔️ Paid a contractor $2,400 for services? Generally a 1099-NEC. Paid someone $1,800? Generally not required.
✔️ Paid by credit card or through a payment network? That's reported on a 1099-K, not your 1099-NEC.
✔️ 1099-NECs for 2026 are due to contractors and the IRS on Feb. 1, 2027, because Jan. 31 falls on a Sunday.

Collect W-9s now, while people still answer emails. Our guide walks through who gets one and how to file.
captions.youtube_title: 1099-NEC Rule for 2026 Payments: The New $2,000 Threshold
captions.youtube_description: For payments made in 2026, Form 1099-NEC is generally required when you pay a contractor $2,000 or more for services (it was $600). Card and payment-network payments go on Form 1099-K instead. 2026 forms are due to contractors and the IRS on Feb. 1, 2027, since Jan. 31 falls on a Sunday.

sources.fact: For tax years beginning after 2025 the NEC reporting threshold is $2,000 (Box 1a: NEC of $2,000 or more); instructions Rev. 12/2026, read 2026-10-24
Prior threshold: 'Enter nonemployee compensation (NEC) of $600 or more' (Rev. April 2025 instructions)
Credit/payment card and third-party network payments are reported on Form 1099-K, not 1099-NEC
Furnish and file 1099-NEC by January 31; a due date on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next business day (Jan. 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so Feb. 1, 2027)
